note: Bot numbers from scripts/balance/sim.ts, not human ones: they say whether the keep moved, not how hard it is. Bands are deliberately loose so they catch accidental large drift, not tuning. A deliberate balance change is expected to fail npm run balance:check and to update this file (measured and bands) in the same pull request. Rates and HP are percentages (death rate is of runs that reached the floor; HP left is the median over floors cleared); run length is seconds. With 30 runs one run is 3.3 points of a rate. Plan 017 (2026-09-28): floors became chains of sealed chambers joined by doors, with no corridors or dead ends to walk. Every policy's run is shorter (default 268.5s -> 147.1s) and its run-length band moved with it. One real change besides: the crossbow special escapes 80% of runs, not 100%, and dies on floor 3 in 20% - a sealed chamber has no corridor to back into, which is how a crossbow outlasted everything - so its escape and floor-3 death bands were widened to hold what was measured, not tuned back. Plan 018 (2026-09-29): the shieldbearer, pyre and bonecaller are dealt (floors 2, 2 and 3), the sim models their shield, fire and reserve, and the measured block was re-taken. Every band still holds, so none moved. The bots barely notice the three kinds: no death is theirs, and the pyre's fire is 4.6% of the default knight's damage taken. The measured drift is run length (default 147.1s -> 148.6s and similar for the others) and the crossbow special (escape 80 -> 90, floor-3 deaths 20 -> 10; one run in ten is one chamber's luck at 30 runs, and the cause was not chased) Sim parity fix (2026-09-30): a knight's bolt now pushes along its own heading, as the game does, instead of the knight-to-body line, which changes which bolts a shield turns; only two measured values moved (weak run length 128.2s -> 128.3s, special-crossbow 219.2s -> 222.8s) and no band moved). Plan 019 Stage C (2026-10-01): no chamber pays an arm any more, so the chamber that did keeps the mend or purse it was dealt (the generator draws everything it drew, so every spawn and prop is where it was) and the sim's door preference (cache, then mend, then arm) now sees one more mend or purse door per floor and no arm door. That chamber also pays a heal of 30 or a purse of 60 where it paid the 12-point top-up. Every band still holds, so none moved; measured was re-taken. The drift: weak escapes 83.3% (was 86.7) with floor-3 deaths 10.7% (was 7.1), special-crossbow escapes 93.3% (was 90.0) with floor-3 deaths 6.7% (was 10.0), special-flask runs 196.7s (was 202.7), and the rest within a second. At 30 runs one run is 3.3 points, so these are one or two runs of the losing policies and no cause beyond the door order was chased. Plan 019 Stage D (2026-10-02): two policies join, `meta-max` (the default knight) and `weak-meta-max` (the weak one), each with every upgrade bought ("meta": "max", resolved through dungeon-meta.ts so it cannot go stale: Deep Lungs 3, Whetted Start 2, Keen Eye, Second Tide; the arm is still the policy's own). They exist to price what the shop does to a knight, not to guard a retune. Measured at 30 runs from seed 1: meta-max escapes 100% in 115.7s (default 100% in 148.6s), weak-meta-max escapes 100% in 97.5s (weak 83.3% in 127.9s, floor-3 deaths 10.7% to 0). That is the design finding the plan's stop rule names: 100% is above the 98% the stop rule allows, and 300 runs agree (weak-meta-max 300 of 300, weak 89.3%). So these bands record where the bot sits and are NOT an acceptance of it; the operator decides whether the upgrades or the keep move first (the difficulty pass), and until then the bands are deliberately the same width as the default policy's. Whetted Start is nearly all of it: the weak knight with that one upgrade escapes 150 of 150 and runs 25% quicker. Prices set and Whetted Start corrected (2026-10-02, operator): Stage A had built Whetted Start as STRIKE_BONUS (a whole blade, +4) per rank, two ranks, where D4 asked for +1 per rank; it is now one rank of +1 (WHET_STRIKE), so the ablation above measured an upgrade eight times the size of the one that ships. Re-measured: meta-max 100% in 145.7s (was 115.7s); weak-meta-max still escapes 100% but its median HP left falls to 89.7 / 85.2 / 78.7 (was 100 on every floor) in 123.8s (was 97.5s), so its HP bands are now the weak policy's own widths, since that is the knight it is. Escape is still above the stop rule's 98%: the difficulty pass is still owed. Plan 021 Stage B (2026-10-03): every stair hall now holds a boss, the Drowned Captain (60 vitality; swing, swing, sweep, and below half a pounce), where it held two or three wardens, and the sim deals and models it. Its numbers are D7's hypothesis and Stage F's to tune against D9, so nothing is tuned here, and measured was re-taken. The Captain lowers the bots' vitality and kills almost none of them yet: weak escapes 90.0% (was 83.3, one run in a floor-2 death and a floor-3 death changed hands), special-crossbow 90.0% (was 93.3), default and weak-meta-max stay at 100%. The two bands that no longer held are the weak knight's median vitality left on floors 1 and 2 (70.0 and 69.6, bands [78, 100] and [70, 100]), because a knight that never dodges now meets the Captain's 24-damage swings before the stair; both minimums moved to 60 and no other band moved. A bot that strikes every frame fells the Captain in seconds, far under D9's 25-60 s: that is Stage F's finding to act on. Plan 021 Stages C and D (2026-10-03): the pool holds four bosses (the Captain, the Pyre Mother, the Tide Hound and the Bastion, dealt per run, never the same on floors one and two) and the floor-two boss is no longer the Captain on most seeds; the sim models the Mother's fan and scatter (and steps out of a marked ring), the Hound's chained pounce and the Bastion's shield breaking in its second phase, and measured was re-taken. Every band still holds, so none moved. The shifts: special-crossbow escapes 80.0% (was 90.0) with a floor-1 death (3.3, was 0) and a floor-2 death (6.9, was 0), three of its six non-escapes to the Bastion, whose shield turns the crossbow's bolts aside from the front (a ranged arm has no answer to it but the flank, which is the design; the band [60, 100] holds it); meta-max escapes 96.7% (was 100), one run stuck on floor two for the whole 480 s because a knight and the Mother, each standing on a cell boundary, trade a pursuit tie every frame (a sim artifact, see progress.md); weak-meta-max floor 1 and 2 vitality left 83.1 and 84.5 (were 79.7 and 75.5), and weak escape stays 90.0. The default knight still escapes 100% with 100% vitality left on every floor and the weak knight's 90.0%: no pool boss kills a bot that dodges, and the weakest bot loses most vitality to the Bastion (60 and 69 in a duel), the Hound (54, 63), the Captain (48, 56) and least to the Mother (22, 26). Bot boss fights still run 5 to 12 s against D9's 25 to 60 s: that is Stage F's to tune (HP and damage), reported and not retuned here.
